# Plan: Add Context Plumbing Throughout the CLI

## Context

`main.go` creates a cancellable context (`context.WithCancel`) and passes it to Cobra via `rootCmd.ExecuteContext(ctx)`. However, no command retrieves it via `cmd.Context()`. Instead, ~120+ production code locations create `context.Background()`, losing cancellation support from SIGINT/SIGTERM and any parent context values.

## Goal

Thread the root context from `main.go` through the entire call chain, replacing `context.Background()` with the properly propagated context. This enables signal-based cancellation to propagate to git operations, checkpoint writes, and other long-running work.

fix(hooks): bound the first-checkpoint git-status subprocess and close review gaps

Adversarial-review follow-ups to the status-walk budget:

- Bound the first-checkpoint `git status --porcelain -z -uall` subprocess
  in collectChangedFiles with the same (now exported)
  gitrepo.StatusWalkBudget via context.WithTimeout — after a go-git
  breach the hook could otherwise still outlive the agent's timeout
  stuck in an undeadlined child git. On expiry the child is killed and
  the error wraps gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded; the turn-end and
  subagent-end handlers recognize the sentinel from SaveStep /
  SaveTaskStep and warn-and-skip the checkpoint instead of failing the
  hook.

- Cover the cross-process marker shape the same-process test could not
  reach: turn start breaches and writes UntrackedScanSkipped, turn end
  runs with a fresh latch and a healthy walk — the changes.New guards
  in the lifecycle handlers are the sole protection against claiming
  every pre-existing untracked file, and deleting either guard now
  fails a test (verified by mutation).

- Give `entire session adopt` an explicit unbounded walk
  (detectFileChangesUnbounded): it is a user-attended command, so a
  slow-but-healthy repo should finish rather than error at the
  hook-path budget.

- State explicitly (comment at untrackedFilesOrSkip) that the
  pre-prompt/pre-task scans fail open on ANY error, not just budget
  breaches — the old fail-hook behavior on status errors was the bug.

git: open repositories with alternates-aware storage

Shared clones can store required objects only through .git/objects/info/alternates. Several checkpoint paths opened repositories with plain go-git storage, so local-only checkpoint commits reachable through alternates could look missing. That made metadata rebase and push paths silently skip checkpoint data and leave remote checkpoint branches incomplete.

Add a gitrepo package that centralizes repository opening, resolves linked worktree .git/commondir layouts, and wires go-git's AlternatesFS so multiple and nested alternates are readable. Route repository openings across the CLI and shared test harnesses through that package so go-git sees the same object graph everywhere.

Also close repository handles after use. Upstream go-git requires callers to close repositories to release filesystem storage resources, so the shared opener documents ownership and call sites now defer Close or register test cleanup.

The TestFetchAndRebase_SharedCloneLocalCommitInAlternate confirms that local clones depending on alternates work. It is currently failing. This is due to the AlternateFS not being properly set on go-git. Make the test pass without changing the test. A copy of the go-git code can be found at ../go-git.

`git init` in $HOME with no .gitignore) the walk ground for hours in
hook processes that outlived the agent's ~60s hook timeout — two
zombies at ~1.8GB RSS, one with 25 CPU-minutes — while the failure
stayed completely silent: no session state, no checkpoint, no log line.

Add gitrepo.StatusWithBudget: a 20s wall-clock budget (headroom under
the agent timeout for the rest of the capture path) enforced by a
goroutine+select wrapper that abandons the walk on breach — the
orphaned goroutine dies with the one-shot hook process, which is the
point. On breach it returns an error wrapping
gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded, emits an actionable Warn naming the
repo root, elapsed, budget, and consequence, and latches a
process-local flag so no later walk in the same hook process re-enters
the worktree (the turn-start hook walks twice: pre-prompt capture and
prompt attribution).

Route the agent-hook call sites through it — DetectFileChanges
(turn-end, subagent-end, PostTodo), the pre-prompt/pre-task untracked
scans, and the prompt-attribution walk — and make the pre-prompt/
pre-task captures fail open on status errors instead of failing the
hook: capture proceeds with transcript-derived data, and a new
UntrackedScanSkipped marker tells the paired end-hook to skip new-file
detection so pre-existing untracked files are not misattributed to the
agent. Git-hook paths (post-commit condensation) never call Status;
review/rewind keep the unbounded Status since a user is actively
waiting there.
